meta.title: RADIUS Lab · NCKU Civil Engineering
meta.description: RADIUS Lab — resilient infrastructure through data, sensing, and computation. Department of Civil Engineering, National Cheng Kung University.

hero.subtitle: RADIUS builds the data, models, and sensing that let infrastructure survive the hazards of a changing world.

items.title: Infrastructure resilience
items.desc: Modeling how bridges, pipelines, and networks degrade and recover under extreme events.

items.title: Structural health monitoring
items.desc: Turning sensor data into early, actionable signals of structural change and risk.

items.title: Hazard & climate risk
items.desc: Quantifying how earthquakes, floods, and a changing climate reshape infrastructure risk.

items.title: Data-driven resilience assessment of aging bridge networks
Physics-informed learning for structural health monitoring
Digital twins for post-earthquake infrastructure recovery
Bayesian damage detection under environmental variability

pi.name: Chia-Wei (Joe) Hsu
pi.bio: Joe leads RADIUS in the Department of Civil Engineering at National Cheng Kung University. His group works at the intersection of structural engineering, sensing, and data science to make infrastructure more resilient to natural hazards.

items.text: RADIUS is awarded a new grant to study resilient bridge networks.
Welcome to two new graduate students joining the lab.
Our paper on physics-informed monitoring is accepted to MSSP.
Joe gives an invited talk at the National Earthquake Engineering Symposium.

join.title: We're looking for curious people who like hard problems.
join.text: We welcome prospective graduate students, postdocs, and undergraduates from civil engineering, mechanics, and data science. If our questions excite you, get in touch.
